chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the traveller who prays behind the resident, he said: He prays two rak'at and proceeds wherever he wishes.

key_terms.الْمُسَافِرِ: The traveller (one on a journey with reduced prayer)
key_terms.الْمُقِيمِ: The resident (one not on a journey with full prayer)

ai.seo_question: How does a traveller complete their prayer when praying behind a resident imam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural flexibility for a traveller (musafir) joining a resident (muqim) in prayer, specifically addressing the scenario where the traveller prays behind the resident. It establishes that the traveller performs two rak'at and then departs or completes the prayer independently, highlighting the practical leniency granted to travellers in Shia jurisprudence to accommodate their transient status without being bound by the full duration of the resident's prayer.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the traveller praying Salāt behind the staying one (non-traveller). Heasws said: ‘He should pray two Rak’at, and he can move (away) wherever he so desires to’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a traveler if he can perform Salah (prayer) behind a non-traveler.
He (the Imam) said, ‘After performing two Rak‘at, he then can move away whenever he wants.’”
